subject: food-technology
topicDisplay: Food Safety Food Science And Special Diets
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Why should you avoid washing raw chicken under a running tap before cooking?
options: It can splash and spread bacteria around the kitchen
It cooks the chicken too quickly
questions.explain: Washing raw chicken splashes bacteria such as campylobacter onto surfaces, hands and other foods.

questions.q: Heat transferred through the movement of currents in a liquid or gas is called:
questions.explain: Convection transfers heat by the circulation of currents in liquids or gases, as in boiling water or an oven.

questions.q: Which condition is most strongly linked to a long-term diet high in saturated fat and salt?
questions.explain: A diet high in saturated fat and salt raises the risk of coronary heart disease.

questions.q: Why does whisking egg white before adding it to a mixture help a cake to rise?
options: It traps air which expands on heating
questions.explain: Whisking aerates the egg white, trapping air bubbles that expand when heated to raise the mixture.

questions.q: Type 2 diabetes is most associated with which dietary and lifestyle factor?
options: Being overweight and a diet high in sugar
questions.explain: Type 2 diabetes is strongly linked to being overweight and a diet high in sugar and energy.

questions.q: Which mineral is most important for building strong bones and teeth?
questions.explain: Calcium is essential for the formation and maintenance of strong bones and teeth.

questions.q: Dextrinisation is the browning of which substance under dry heat?
questions.explain: Dextrinisation is the breakdown and browning of starch when exposed to dry heat, as in toasting bread.

questions.q: Some bacteria are hard to destroy by normal cooking because they can:
options: Be killed instantly at room temperature
Form heat-resistant spores and produce toxins
questions.explain: Some bacteria form heat-resistant spores, and certain toxins they produce are not destroyed by normal cooking.

questions.q: The '4 Cs' of food safety are cleaning, cooking, chilling and:
questions.explain: The 4 Cs are Cleaning, Cooking, Chilling and avoiding Cross-contamination.

questions.q: Which nutrient is needed to carry oxygen around the body as part of haemoglobin?
questions.explain: Iron is an essential component of haemoglobin, which transports oxygen in red blood cells.

questions.q: When self-raising flour is used, the raising agent releases which gas to make a cake rise?
questions.explain: Baking powder in self-raising flour produces carbon dioxide gas, which expands and raises the mixture.

questions.q: A 'best-before' date mainly refers to a food's:
options: Quality, such as flavour and texture
questions.explain: A best-before date relates to quality; food may still be safe to eat after this date but may be lower quality.

questions.q: Which type of food is classed as 'high-risk' for food poisoning?
questions.explain: High-risk foods are moist, protein-rich, ready-to-eat foods such as cooked meat and cooked rice.

questions.q: The temperature range known as the 'danger zone', in which bacteria multiply most rapidly, is:
questions.explain: The danger zone is 5-63C, the range in which bacteria multiply most quickly.

questions.q: Caramelisation is the browning that occurs when which ingredient is heated to a high temperature?
questions.explain: Caramelisation is the browning and flavour change that happens when sugar is heated to a high temperature.

questions.q: Bacteria in the danger zone can roughly double in number every:
questions.explain: In ideal conditions bacteria can divide approximately every 10-20 minutes, so numbers rise rapidly.

questions.q: Combining two low biological value plant proteins to provide all essential amino acids is called:
questions.explain: Complementary proteins, such as beans on toast, combine different LBV proteins so all essential amino acids are supplied.

questions.q: Which group of vitamins is mainly needed to help release energy from food?
questions.explain: B vitamins act as part of the enzyme systems that release energy from carbohydrates, fats and proteins.

questions.q: Which of the following is a biological raising agent?
questions.explain: Yeast is a biological raising agent that produces carbon dioxide through fermentation to make dough rise.

questions.q: The browning of the surface of bread or toast as starch is exposed to dry heat is called:
questions.explain: Dextrinisation is the browning of starch under dry heat, as seen on toast and baked bread crusts.

questions.q: When an egg is heated and sets from a runny liquid to a firm solid, this change is called:
questions.explain: Heat causes egg proteins to denature and then coagulate, setting them into a solid.

questions.q: Overcooking green vegetables in lots of water for a long time mainly causes the loss of which nutrient?
questions.explain: Vitamin C is water-soluble and heat-sensitive, so prolonged boiling destroys and leaches it away.
